outcome.technical: MECHANISM: (i), the call's own start record. The sweep-lane Pre already writes _config.record_call_start for every Bash/MCP call before the switch is consulted, with the call's tool_use_id; it now also carries the switch as that Pre read it (record_call_start(..., journal_on=) under _config.CALL_JOURNAL_KEY 'journalOn', same single write; read back by the new _config.call_journal_on(root, cfg, data, call), True only when the record names that call id and holds True; call_start refactored onto a shared _call_record, behaviour unchanged). The edit lane needs no new state: its Pre writes a slot naming the call (CALL_ID_KEY) and only with the journal on, so a slot naming the Post's id IS that call's reading 'on' (new _own_slot; _slot_start now uses it). Chosen over (ii) because (ii) would write slots and snapshot files while the switch is off, and would still need binding to the call id; (i) adds no read, no write, no process and no listing to any Pre. WHAT THE PRE DOES WHILE OFF: before - wrote the call-start record (swept tools only), then returned. After - the same one write, now with journalOn false in it, then returns; no slot, no read. This is not the plugin working after being told to stop: the record is written whatever the switch says because guard-bash-writes reads its moment, and the reading in it lets the Post do less. POST: journal-writes.py _swept_rows (line 1286) returns before any sweep when the switch is off now and _own_switch_on is False - no slot read, none written (before: read slot + snapshot per root); post_rows (line 1507) returns [] when off now unless the target is the trail tree's own config AND _own_slot. The mark line on the edit lane lost its now-redundant rel test (the return above holds it). A PAYLOAD WITH NO tool_use_id marks nothing on either lane (call_journal_on(call=None) -> False; _own_slot needs an id). Installed Claude Code 2.1.327 sends tool_use_id on both events (strings of the binary: hook_event_name:"PreToolUse",tool_name:e,tool_input:o,tool_use_id:n and hook_event_name:"PostToolUse",...,tool_response:u,tool_use_id:n).
